topics.name: Decision Tree Splitting Criterion (Entropy & Information Gain)
topics.description: Computation of node impurity using entropy, calculation of information gain for each candidate feature, and selection of the split that maximally reduces impurity. Includes the formulas Entropy(S) = −Σ pᵢ log₂(pᵢ) and Information Gain = Entropy(parent) − Σ (|child|/|parent|)·Entropy(child).

topics.name: Overfitting and Pruning in Decision Trees
topics.description: Causes of overfitting in fully grown trees, the instability of trees to small data changes, and strategies to control tree depth, minimum sample counts, or use post‑hoc pruning to improve generalisation.

topics.name: Random Forest Ensemble Mechanics
topics.description: Construction of a forest via bootstrap sampling of training rows, random selection of feature subsets at each split (typically √p), independent deep tree growth, and aggregation of predictions by majority vote (classification) or averaging (regression). Includes discussion of out‑of‑bag (OOB) samples as an internal validation set.

topics.name: Feature‑Importance Ranking in Random Forests
topics.description: How the ensemble provides a built‑in measure of each feature’s contribution to prediction accuracy, often derived from the decrease in impurity or permutation importance across all trees.

topics.name: K‑Means Clustering Objective and Convergence (Lloyd’s Algorithm)
topics.description: Iterative process of assigning points to the nearest centroid, updating centroids as the mean of assigned points, and minimizing the total within‑cluster sum of squares (WCSS). Guarantees that WCSS never increases, leading to convergence to a (possibly local) optimum.

topics.name: Initialization Sensitivity and Choosing k in K‑Means
topics.description: Impact of random centroid initialization on final clusters, risks of poor local minima, and the need to pre‑select the number of clusters k. Highlights that k‑means does not infer k automatically and that multiple restarts or methods (e.g., elbow) are often used.

topics.name: Model Trade‑offs: Interpretability vs. Accuracy vs. Stability
topics.description: Comparison of Decision Trees, Random Forests, and K‑Means across dimensions such as interpretability (high for trees, medium for forests, low for clustering), variance/overfitting risk, training speed, and suitability for different problem types (supervised vs. unsupervised).
